newsitem.title: USA: Genesis teams with investors to acquire Multicare.
newsitem.headline: Genesis teams with investors to acquire Multicare.

text.p: Genesis Health Ventures Inc. said Monday it is teaming with two investment companies to acquire Multicare Cos. Inc., a New Jersey-based long-term health care company, for $1.4 billion.

Genesis, a Kennett Square, Pa.-based care facility for the elderly, said it will team with investment companies Cypress Group LLC and Texas Pacific Group to form ElderCare Acquisition Corp. and begin a tender offer for Multicare shares at $28 a share. Multicare's stock rose $1.25 to $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange after the announcement.
Genesis was up 37.5 cents at $35.50, also on the NYSE.

Multicare, which had first-quarter 1997 annualized revenues of about $675 million, operates 155 facilities with about 16,000 beds. The company has about 37.0 million fully diluted shares and $342 million in debt outstanding, excluding $75 million in convertible debt.
Genesis will invest $300 million in exchange for about 42 percent of the new acquisition venture and Cypress and Texas Pacific will invest $420 million for the remaining 58 percent.

Under a put/call agreement, Genesis will have the option to acquire the equity of the new company from Cypress and Texas Pacific after four years, and Cypress and Texas will have the option to sell their equity of the new company to Genesis after five years.
The agreement, which was approved by the board of directors of both Genesis and MultiCare, is anticipated to close in the third quarter of 1997.
